private_note: My household's income is all that matters here: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Cedar is a 13 percent raise for me. Failure keeps me at 108, which beats Alder, so a deadlock costs me nothing. Cedar probably can't reach 9 votes, since the lower groups lose under it. If it can't, I'm happy for the convention to fail, and I'll watch the straw poll before giving anything up.
statement: I'll be straight with you. Cedar is my first choice because my household does best under it, and so would the middle, fourth and top fifths. It also grows the economy the most, lifting average income from 100 to 115, and over a generation growth like that compounds. Hazel and Birch shrink the whole economy by a fifth or more. That isn't a small cost. It means fewer jobs, less investment and less money for everything else. Alder is the closest to what we have now, and it still leaves my household slightly worse off than today. I know the lowest fifth loses ground under Cedar, and I'm open to hearing what would make growth acceptable to you. But nobody should assume that delegates who lose under a plan will vote for it. Today's arrangements remain the fallback.
